headline: Every can checked, not a sample.
label: #F4EAD5
heroLede: With several beers in the same can size and the line running fast, the label and the date are what keep each run right. Here's what a camera check could look like on your canning line. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks every can has its end on and seated, with no visible damage around the seam. It looks at what can be seen from outside, so it adds to your seam checks rather than replacing them.
labelLede: A pacific ale and a pale ale in the same can size look much the same at line speed. The camera checks every can carries the right label for the run, straight and intact.
codeLede: The best-before and batch code has to be right and readable on every can. The system reads the printed code and compares it with the beer and date set at changeover.
objectLede: Can ends, label backing and carton offcuts can all end up on the conveyor. The camera over the belt spots anything that should not be there before it reaches a pack.

vocab.alert: Four ends not seated in fifteen minutes. Check the seamer.
